title: The Endless Smile
premise: Xanthe Lockridge, a meticulous property surveyor, is hired to appraise the derelict Halloway house before its demolition, and discovers the property responds to her measurements—rooms shifting to falsify her reports. When the excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, she learns the house was built as a cage for something the founding family invited in and never released, sustained by decades of documented lies in the county records. As night falls and the crew vanishes one by one, Xanthe realizes the entity feeds on complicity: everyone who profited from the cover-up belongs to it. She survives until sunrise by burning her own appraisal—the document that would have legally enabled the demolition—and instead files the truth, breaking the seal from outside, though the ending leaves ambiguous whether she escaped or was simply invited to stay.
about_author: Edmund Reyes is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent eleven years cataloging condemned properties across the Rust Belt before turning to horror. He writes about paperwork as haunted ground, and lives quietly in a town whose records he refuses to discuss.

chapters.title: The House That Measures Back
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Arriving at the Halloway house, she documents every room with obsessive care, but her laser measurements return impossible numbers that change when re-checked, and her photographs show rooms she never entered. The emotional beat is professional unease curdling into personal affront—her instruments, her identity, are being lied to.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Xanthe and crew foreman Dale Okafor's POV alternates. The excavation unearths an iron door bolted shut from within; inside, they find the founding family's bones arranged around a ledger of deeds. That evening, two crew members don't clock out. The beat shifts from curiosity to dread as Xanthe realizes the house has been waiting for someone with legal authority over it.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Signed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV through the night. Trapped by doors that only open inward, she reads the ledger and understands: each signature on the property's history was an invitation renewed, including the demolition permit bearing her firm's letterhead. Crew members vanish as their names surface. Climactic beat: she confronts the entity wearing the faces of past surveyors, all smiling endlessly, offering her belonging if she signs.

chapters.title: Filed Under Truth
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV at dawn. Refusing to sign, she burns her appraisal in the hearth—the act of withdrawal that starves the invitation—and photographs the ledger with intent to file it publicly, turning documentation from prayer into weapon. The door opens outward at sunrise. Resolution carries cost: her measurements of herself no longer add up, and the final image suggests the smile followed her home.
